parts.article:
Part three.

You will hear two business students called Emma and Nick preparing for their presentation on the topic of how jobs might change in the future.

First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-four.

Now listen carefully and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.

Okay, Nick. The title of our presentation is How Jobs Might Change in the Future. Shall we look at the research we've done so far?

I was just watching an interview with Alex Coburn.

Go on.

He talked about a company with a call center for dealing with complaints. Instead of following a script with a list of questions they had to ask, the call center employees were told they could deal with complaints however they wanted, which went down well with them.

That's not a common approach these days.

But apparently it worked. Customers were happier with the new methods.

Really? That's certainly not the result you'd expect. We'll definitely have to use that example.

Maybe.

What about Jerry Kaplan's report? He argues there'll be plenty of jobs not suitable for machines. Like, a machine might be able to diagnose your disease, but patients will always want to talk face-to-face with their doctor. I suppose it's something to do with the fact that a human can empathize, but a machine can't.

Right.

Now, there's that article called The Human Cloud. It describes the growing numbers of people being employed as contractors to do online tasks at a distance. While that could be good for the companies, they can choose the most expert people available, and they get cheap labor and no costs except wages. But for the workers, it may mean less money.

On the other hand, I love the idea of working from home and at a time that suits.

It's certainly controversial.

Another article was the one looking at how employers will use technology to record what their employees are doing.

So awful. Cameras in the workplace, checking on where you are, software that tells your boss who you've been emailing.

When we talk about this, I want to make clear how this affects people's personal privacy. Did you read how some companies are tracking the health of their employees? Surely, workers won't accept that.

Yes, I'd be very surprised if this became common. Too many employees would refuse.

Before you hear the rest of the discussion, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to thirty.

Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to thirty.

Okay. There's some aspects of the presentation we still need to think about.

Yes, there are a few issues. Let's go through them one by one.

Okay.

What about the introduction then?

Well, we've sorted out the content.

Your editing has helped. But don't you think you ought to deliver it rather than me? It's mainly your work.

Okay. So let's do it that way then.

Good.

What about the researcher profiles?

Cathy Bryson and Alex Coburn's backgrounds? I doubt we'll have time to look at them properly during the presentation. I reckon we should just attach that bit to the written report we're giving to the tutor.

So cut it?

Let's rehearse the whole presentation and see if it's necessary.

What about the section on automation?

Aren't you happy with it?

I'm thinking I haven't really given equal attention to the pros and cons.

I should start again.

Well, let's have a bit more of a think about it. You don't want to rush into a big job like that.

Another thing is the section on workplace structure. I think we've got some good points, but...

We're only using one particular company as a case study. We need to source some other situations as supporting material.

So perhaps we could both do a search and compare notes.

And choose the most interesting cases.

And the section on tracking technology, are we happy with that?

It would definitely benefit from some photos.

Hang on. There's no point using images just for decoration. We need to think about whether they'd serve any real purpose.

Fair enough. Let's make a decision on that at a later stage. And that interview we did with the company manager.

Yes, we were lucky she gave us her time.

But I just want to be sure we wrote everything down accurately. I wouldn't like to misrepresent her views.

Maybe I should type up that section and send it to her so she can confirm whether or not it's correct.

Yes, that's a good idea. Go ahead.

Sounds like a plan.

Okay, and we-

That is the end of part three.

You now have thirty seconds to check your answers to part three.

questions.question: What do the students find surprising about the way that complaints were dealt with at the call centre?

analyses.content: 男生提到客户对新的处理方式感到更满意，这正是让两人感到意想不到（surprising）的结果。
你可能会因为听到录音里说这种方式“went down well with them”（员工很乐意）而错选B，但员工并没有缺乏热情，而真正的“惊喜”在于后续明确提到的“客户反馈”。
But apparently, it worked. Customers were happier with the new methods. Really? That's certainly not the result you'd expect.

questions.question: What does Emma say about the report by Jerry Kaplan?

analyses.content: 男生总结报告内容时明确指出，机器无法像人类一样产生共情，这是机器做不到的局限性。
你可能会因为听到“diagnose your disease”等机器能做的事情而误选，但录音的转折和最后的话题重点落在了“机器不能（can't）”的缺陷上。

What about Jerry Kaplan's report? He argues there'll be plenty of jobs not suitable for machines. Like a machine might be able to diagnose your disease, but patients will always want to talk face-to-face with their doctor. I suppose it's something to do with the fact that a human can empathize, but a machine can't.

questions.question: What is Nick’s reaction to the article The Human Cloud?

analyses.content: Nick明确表示自己很喜欢这种能在家办公且时间自己说了算的想法，即支持员工拥有更大的灵活性。
你可能会因为前面大段谈论“对公司的好处（节省成本）”或者“对工人的坏处（钱变少）”而走神，没跟上Nick随后用“On the other hand”表达的转折态度。

Now, there's that article called The Human Cloud. It describes the growing numbers of people being employed as contractors to do online tasks at a distance. While that could be good for the companies, they can choose the most expert people available, and they get cheap labor and no costs except wages. But for the workers, it may mean less money. On the other hand, I love the idea of working from home and at a time that suits.

analyses.content: 两人一致认为员工绝对“won't accept that（不会接受）”并且“would refuse（会拒绝）”，即员工会强烈反对这种监控技术。
你可能会因为录音里提到“Cameras in the workplace”相关的词汇而错选A，但这里的核心是两人在探讨员工对“追踪健康信息”的不满和抗拒态度。
Did you read how some companies are tracking the health of their employees? Surely, workers won't accept that. Yes, I'd be very surprised if this became common. Too many employees would refuse.

analyses.content: 女生建议让男生来做展示（deliver it rather than me），这直接对应了讨论“谁来负责展示（which of them will present it）”的选项H。
你可能会因为听到“sorted out the content”或“editing”而产生干扰联想，忽略了最后拍板的核心决定“deliver it”是指决定演讲的人选。

What about the introduction then? Well, we've sorted out the content. Your editing has helped. But don't you think you ought to deliver it rather than me? It's mainly your work. Okay. So let's do it that way then.
两人认为演讲时没时间好好看研究员简介，提议“cut it（删掉）”并移到书面报告中，对应“完全删掉（removed completely）”的选项B。
你可能只听到了“attach that bit to the written report”但没反应过来，这里的言外之意就是将其从现有的“展示（presentation）”环节中移除。

What about the researcher profiles? Cathy Bryson and Alex Coburn's backgrounds? I doubt we'll have time to look at them properly during the presentation. I reckon we should just attach that bit to the written report we're giving to the tutor. So cut it? Let's rehearse the whole presentation and see if it's necessary.
男生觉得自己没处理好这部分的优缺点，直言“I should start again（我应该重头再来）”，对应完全重写（completely re-written）的选项D。
你可能会觉得录音里两人还要再商量（have a bit more of a think about it），但题目问的是他们发现的“缺陷/问题”，男生点出的根本问题就是要“重写”。

What about the section on automation? Aren't you happy with it? I'm thinking I haven't really given equal attention to the pros and cons. I should start again. Well, let's have a bit more of a think about it. You don't wanna rush into a big job like that.
男生提出目前的案例太单一，需要“source some other situations（找些其他情况）”，对应寻找更多补充例子（further examples）的选项G。
你可能会因为听到“one particular company”而纠结，但紧接着的“source some other situations”以及“choose the most interesting cases”才是针对问题提出的具体改进举措。

Another thing is the section on workplace structure. I think we've got some good points, but- We're only using one particular company as a case study. We need to source some other situations as supporting material. So perhaps we could both do a search and compare notes. And choose the most interesting cases.
两人在讨论这部分是否需要加入照片（photos/images）以及这些视觉元素是否能起到实际作用，对应“视觉材料是否有帮助”的选项E。
你可能会听到“decoration”或“real purpose”而过度理解，实际上他们通篇争论的核心就是“照片（visuals）到底需不需要加”。

And the section on tracking technology, are we happy with that? It would definitely benefit from some photos. Hang on. There's no point using images just for decoration. We need to think about whether they'd serve any real purpose. Fair enough. Let's make a decision on that at a later stage, and that interview we did with the company manager.
男生担心自己错误传达了经理的观点，提出要把写下来的内容发给对方“confirm whether or not it's correct（确认是否正确）”，对应信息核对（information needs to be checked）的选项F。
你可能会因为听到前面说“lucky she gave us her time”而觉得没问题并因此走神，错过了转折后“be sure we wrote everything down accurately”的真正核对诉求。

...and that interview we did with the company manager. Yes. We were lucky she gave us her time. But I just want to be sure we wrote everything down accurately. I wouldn't like to misrepresent her views. Maybe I should type up that section and send it to her, so she can confirm whether or not it's correct. Yes, that's a good idea. Go ahead.
